author: Rumi
story:
Rather than offering a polite platitude, this observation challenges how we navigate our inner lives. Genuine love is not a transaction where you keep score of who gave what; it is a state of being where you extend warmth and goodwill without needing to control the other person.

Across his life and work, Rumi saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. The biggest barrier to deep connection is never external; it is our own fear of rejection. We build armor around our hearts to avoid pain, but that same armor ends up locking out the warmth and intimacy we crave.
reflectionPrompt: How can you integrate the essence of this wisdom into one specific decision or encounter today?
